Creamy Vegetable Stew with Lentils (One Pot)

ByBecca Heyes September 14, 2026September 14, 2026

Creamy Vegetable Stew with Lentils

Total time: 1 hour hour 10 minutes minutes
Servings: 5 portions
No ratings yet

This creamy vegetable stew is the perfect vegetarian comfort food - packed with veggies and lentils, in a tasty creamy sauce.

I’ll take just about any excuse to get my enormous casserole pot out of the cupboard, and this creamy vegetable stew is a very good one! It’s an easy one pot dinner that’s packed with colourful vegetables and hearty lentils, all simmered together in a wonderfully creamy, flavour-packed sauce.

This is the kind of meal that makes a pile of vegetables feel seriously irresistible, especially when you serve it with plenty of crusty bread and butter for dipping into that delicious sauce. Perfect comfort food!

🥗 Ingredients

Here’s what you’ll need to make this creamy vegetable stew recipe.

Detailed ingredient quantities (in both US and UK recipe formats) can be found in the printable recipe card.

I’ll admit, the ingredients list for this veggie stew is a little longer than the majority of my recipes – but when one of the recipe steps is essentially ‘add all of the ingredients to the pot’, it doesn’t feel like too much of a hardship.

  • potatoes – I left mine unpeeled because I enjoy the skins (and because it’s easier!). Any potato will work, although a floury potato will break down into the sauce more than a waxy potato will do, so choose depending on your preference.
  • vegetables – I used leek, carrots, runner beans (stringless beans), frozen peas, and frozen sweetcorn.
  • dried lentils – brown or green. Red lentils will also be tasty, although as they break down a lot more when cooking than brown or green lentils do, you’ll end up with quite a different end result. Read more about different kinds of lentils.
  • flour, milk, butter and vegetable stock – to create the creamy base of the sauce.
  • dried herbs, mustard and garlic – to give it lots of flavour.
  • fresh dill – not a herb I use very often! But its fresh flavour works so well to liven up this creamy stew.

🔄 Substitutions

Feel free to swap the vegetables to any others that you prefer – to be honest I’d happily chuck in whatever veggies I have in the fridge. Some ideas:

  • red or white onion
  • parsnips
  • cabbage
  • green beans
  • mushrooms
  • sweet potato
  • celery
  • edamame

etc! Just avoid anything that doesn’t work well with a long cooking time (broccoli or zucchini will turn to mush!)

🔪 Equipment You’ll Need

When I’m making a big casserole like this veggie stew (and lots of my other one pot dinners, like my vegetable potato bake or my shepherd’s pie gnocchi), I love to use my huge Le Creuset pot. Any similar oven-safe pot will do, but I do love my big cast iron pot.

As you might know already, Le Creuset casserole dishes are really rather expensive – mine was a very generous gift many years ago, otherwise I don’t think I would have been able to justify spending so much on a pot. Luckily, you can also buy very similar pots that are a much more budget-friendly and have great reviews:

📝 How to Make Creamy Vegetable Stew

Creamy Vegetable Stew with Lentils

This creamy vegetable stew is the perfect vegetarian comfort food – packed with veggies and lentils, in a tasty creamy sauce.

Allergens: 🧀 Dairy 🍞 Gluten

(please double check all allergens before eating)

Prep Time20 minutes mins
Cook Time50 minutes mins
Total Time1 hour hr 10 minutes mins
Servings: 5 portions
Calories: 414kcal
Recipe by: Becca Heyes

Ingredients

  • 30 g (~ 2 Tablespoons) butter
  • 1 leek, sliced
  • 1 teaspoon minced garlic
  • 2 Tablespoons plain flour
  • 700 g (~ 1 1/2 lb) potatoes, cut into bitesized pieces (I left mine unpeeled)
  • 3 medium carrots, cut into bitesized pieces
  • 225 g (~ 1/2 lb) runner beans (stringless beans), cut into bitesized pieces
  • 200 g (~ 1 cup) dried green or brown lentils
  • 130 g (~ 1 cup) frozen peas
  • 130 g (~ 1 cup) frozen sweetcorn
  • 1 litre (~ 4 cups) vegetable stock
  • 500 ml (~ 2 cups) milk
  • 1 teaspoon dried herbs (I used mixed herbs)
  • 1/2 teaspoon Dijon mustard
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • Small handful fresh dill, roughly chopped
Email yourself this recipe for later!

Instructions
 

  • Melt the butter in a large casserole dish, and add the sliced leek. Sauté for a couple of minutes, until fragrant. Add the garlic, and cook for 1 more minute.
  • Add the flour, and mix well to coat the leek.
  • Add all of the remaining ingredients, except for the dill. Mix well to combine.
  • Cover the pan with a lid, and bring to a simmer. Allow to cook for around 45 minutes to an hour, stirring a few times during cooking. For a thicker stew, you can remove the lid for the second half of the cooking time.
  • To complete the stew, season to taste – I like plenty of black pepper, and if you used low sodium stock, you may also need to add a dash of salt. If you like, you can give the stew a few presses with a potato masher, to help break down the softer vegetables (or leave it chunky if you prefer!).
  • Serve hot, topped with a good scattering of fresh dill. I love to serve this vegetable stew with some bread and butter.

Notes

Since there are quite a few vegetables in this recipe, you might find it easier to prepare (wash, trim, peel, chop) them all before you begin cooking.
You can replace any of the vegetables in this veggie stew with an alternative, e.g. onion, mushrooms, green beans, cabbage, etc.
Any leftovers can be stored in the fridge for up to 3 days, or frozen in an airtight container. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
